sources_read: .qc-cache/kittle-2026-10-09-r5/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx :: Quality Checks row 25 and Internal Quality Checks row 25 (judge_prompts_drive_the_browser)
evidence: All five prompts open with 'Evaluate the live application at http://localhost:3000 using Playwright MCP' (render/constraints/functional/polish prompt.md:1; visual prompt.md:1-2 'Evaluate the rendered application at http://localhost:3000 using Playwright MCP'), and every judge.toml declares the playwright-mcp stdio server (render/constraints/polish/visual judge.toml:11-15, functional:16-20; functional also the verifier restart server :22-27). Prompts forbid non-browser grading: render:2 'Use only rendered browser behavior', constraints:2 'browser-visible behavior and browser network evidence only', functional:23-28 evidence must be gathered in-session, unperformed steps fail, :43-45 replays are in-page from the app origin, 'Never use curl or shell commands', :52 no shell; polish:4,22 'browser-visible evidence', 'not code style'; visual:10-16 rendered presentation only. All treat submitted source as untrusted evidence. First-paint/static-shell guesses are excluded: scored prompts' global gate (functional:11-19, polish:10-18, visual:18-26) says 'a first-paint imitation does not pass' and requires server-backed task data; constraints gate criterion requires posting JUDGE-G1, reload, and readback in a separate context as Harriet. Every functional/polish criterion is an interactive script (posts JUDGE-tagged messages, records/replays requests, multiple browser contexts, reloads, a real restart_app), none answerable from source or memory; visual criteria require resizing to 1440x900/390x844 and viewing post-functional state. app_context.md is injected into every prompt (test.sh:198-200) and gives browser_run_code_unsafe context recipes, all on localhost:3000. Broken-app attempt: a static first-paint mock or local-only storage fails the constraints gate (cross-context readback) and the scored gates. Conforming-alternative attempt: route/cookie/payload-agnostic wording (functional:41,60 'Any endpoint path, payload shape or cookie name is acceptable'; constraints:12) avoids failing a different correct implementation for source-level reasons. Wording matches/extends the frozen template prompts. Limitation (not a defect of this prompt-content row): no full configured judge run exists for these bytes (raw-evidence-index scope), so actual judge tool usage is unmeasured; that gap belongs to the runtime rows.
